summary: Re-pin after a clean rebase onto 9efdab3c (main after #831). Re-verified, not re-stamped: base is the current main tip, all three commits marked, and the diff against the new base is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the diff reviewed at 2319e6c3. Substance carried forward unchanged - ACCEPT after three rounds. Both round-2 blockers are closed and verified with a POSITIVE CONTROL on the prior blocked head: three identical calls on a bounded target give RUN3 = ZERO log records at any level on d306d8d, while HEAD still emits [OMS-CANCEL-UNCONFIRMED] carrying broker_id, last_status and reads_failed, NOT subject to the (target,path) dedup - so the FRTT 2026-08-11 never-silent contract is honoured again. Field spellings aligned: one grep on outcome=refused returns 6 across both populations (2 from #829, 4 direct), and ⭐ the substring-sibling trap was checked explicitly - OMS-CANCEL-DEAD-TARGET-BOUND is NOT a substring of OMS-DIRECT-CANCEL-DEAD-TARGET-BOUND - so a naive grep -c cannot absorb one population into the other. The dedup difference is stated ON THE LINE as emission=once_per_target_path_per_process. Strand analysis executed: a live order with zero terminal refusals still reaches the broker on all four covered paths, each with an in-test one-variable pair, and fail-open holds on all six unknown inputs including a missing row and a None target id - the bound can fire only on positive durable broker evidence. 14 of 16 mutants killed. ⛔ TWO REQUIRED FOLLOW-UP TESTS, both two-liners, over behaviour HEAD already gets right: (1) test_missing_target_row_fails_open_without_inventing_evidence exercises _record_cancel_verify_reports, NOT the gate - inverting that gate to fail CLOSED survives all 2660 tests, and under an inverted gate the verifier would treat 'no row' as 'target is dead', skip the resubmit entirely, and return having logged dead_target_bound=1, which is the FRTT unowned-working-order shape returning while wearing a label that says the opposite; (2) the bounded-drift-abandons-its-intent property is not pinned, because the existing assertion passes on the first UNBOUNDED pass - on a candidate bounded on its FIRST drift pass the mutant leaves intent.status='submitted', a permanently stuck intent that occupies the #644 entry-composition cap and suppresses new entries for that symbol with ZERO broker traffic to reveal it. ⛔ CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER CREDIT: I recorded that the client_order_id-key mutant dies; it dies only against an ORM-identity-map mutant, because the collision test assigns the duplicate coid in memory under no_autoflush while the DB still holds the original. That is NOT a defect - BrokerOrder.client_order_id is unique=True so coid maps 1:1 to BrokerOrder.id in production, making it an equivalent mutant - but the credit was narrower than I stated. ⛔ DEPLOY: this touches oms/service.py, so it needs an OMS restart - the SECOND tonight - with the same pre/post checklist.
